trafficEventSetting.description.noteEnab: Note: Enabling this setting will lead to a higher CPU usage than usual on the NetBird client.
trafficEventSetting.text.trafficEventsIs: Traffic events is an experimental feature. Functionality and behavior may evolve, including changes to how data is collected or reported. Traffic events data retention is limited to 48 hours and capped at a maximum of 50,000 events.
trafficEventSetting.text.enableTrafficEv: Enable traffic events for all peers. This requires NetBird client v0.39 or higher.
trafficEventSetting.text.trafficReportin: Traffic reporting is always enabled in userspace, and this setting only applies to kernel. If enabled, network packets and their size will be counted and reported.
trafficEventSetting.text.selectPeerGroup: Select peer groups for which traffic events will be logged.
trafficEventSetting.text.ifNoGroupIsSele: If no group is selected, logging applies to all peers.
trafficEventsTable.text.trafficEventsHel: Traffic Events help you understand the network activity in your organization. You can see which machines are connecting to each other, and what kind of traffic is flowing between them.
trafficEventsTable.description.weHavenTD: We haven't detected any traffic events yet. This could be because you just enabled the feature, or because there hasn't been any network activity.
trafficEventsTable.searchPlaceholder.sea: Search by ip, port, peer or resource...
trafficEventsPeerTabContent.text.itLooks: It looks like you don't have any traffic events. Traffic events will appear here once clients start connecting to your network.
It looks like you don't have any traffic events. To start receiving traffic events, you need to enable it in your account settings.
trafficEventsPeerTabContent.text.inbound: Here you can see all the inbound traffic events for this peer.
trafficEventsPeerTabContent.text.outboun: Here you can see all the outbound traffic events for this peer.
